newsitem.title: THAILAND: Lower Thai rates sought for weak property sector.
newsitem.headline: Lower Thai rates sought for weak property sector.

text.p: The ailing Thai property sector called on financial institutions to cut mortgage rates and the government to provide more utility services in a joint bid to revive the battered property industry and the overall economy.
"Presently house prices in Thailand are unrealistically expensive because of high mortgage rates of 15-21 percent," said Nakorn Mutusri, managing director of Bangkok Management Realty Co Ltd.
Nakorn told a seminar that private housing costs were marked up to cover utility facilities built by housing developers themselves without assistance from the government.
"The property sector has been sluggish since 1991 and it's about time for the government to step in to help buyers," he said.

He said demand for houses remained high as could be seen from the success of two government-run banks earlier this month in offering house buyers 17.5 billion baht of mortgage loans carrying concessional 9.0-12.75 percent interest rates.

Analysts said earlier that positive impact from the concessional loans was limited as only 12,000-20,000 house buyers benefited from the government support scheme while the market still had about 300,000 surplus housing units.
Atchana Waiquamdee of General Finance and Securities Plc told the same seminar that the property sector slump had affected other sectors in the stock market including banking and finance.
"I think the economic slowdown needs a long time to heal. The government did not take any preventive measures when the economy overheated three or four years ago," Atchana said.
